pr.title: Add project review setup, move, and census
pr.head: 3d18d94eaa3fa0b8e6b08e3c01f9bcd519d7c83e

summary: Adds the first project review commands from the review-scripts plan, so the mechanical steps of review-changes are tested code instead of gh snippets each loop session rebuilds. setup fetches the exact head, including a fork's from pull/<n>/head, into a scratch worktree, records whether the head is trusted, and posts the start comment. move follows a head that moved mid-review by editing that comment in place. census counts the Projector finding threads across every page. release clears a review lock left behind.

review-changes/SKILL.md now runs these commands in place of its snippets, docs/cli.md documents them, and the plan moves to in-progress. publish, which releases the lock in the normal flow, and review.gate are later delivery steps.

cards.title: Shared rules the commands enforce
cards.html:
• No command takes a SHA; each comes from GitHub or the state file.
  • setup works from a source checkout; --repo must match its configured origin. Later commands find the review by --repo or the pull request number.
  • Posts use GH_TOKEN from gh auth token --user <reviewer> for that call alone.
  • The lock is held per pull request and head from setup. It records host, loop, and time, goes stale after a day, and release clears it.
  • --loop keys a per-loop record under loops/<id>/; --rereview marks a re-review.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• 2705222: changes requested, 3 threads (trailing blank line, a lock that was never released, forks refused).
  • 3d18d94: all three fixed and resolved; approved. Suggestions left: census reads at most 50 comments per thread, and nothing releases the lock at publish until publish ships.

groups.title: The review module
groups.kicker: src/projector/review.py: identity, state, lock, setup, move, census
intro: One new module holds the commands and their helpers. setup resolves the checkout and its origin, takes the per-head lock, fetches the head (branch or pull/<n>/head) and base, verifies FETCH_HEAD and the worktree's HEAD against GitHub's SHA, runs trusted_head, posts the start comment with a reviewer token, and writes the state file.

move reads the state, refuses an unmoved head, locks the new head, rechecks trust, edits and re-reads the start comment, and hands the lock over. census pages the review-thread query and keeps threads whose first comment carries projector-finding. release deletes every lock for the pull request.
concepts: The lock lasts from setup until publish, a later step; until then only staleness or release clears it.
Trust follows review-changes: base-repository branch, trusted author, no untrusted commit author.

checks.text: Every SHA the commands act on comes from pull_request() or the state file.
The reviewer token goes only to the posting calls.
trusted_head treats bots and failed permission lookups as untrusted.

files.note: Read take_lock, setup, and move together for the lock lifecycle, and trusted_head against the skill's trust rule.

groups.title: CLI wiring
intro: Adds the review parser with setup, move, census, and release. All four share --repo, --state-dir, --loop, and --json; setup alone takes --checkout, --reviewer, and --rereview. Commands after setup resolve the repository through find_repo.

checks.text: An empty review.username falls through to the authenticated user.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Real Git against a bare origin, fake gh
intro: The tests run git for real against a bare origin and replace run_gh with a recording fake. They cover setup, fork heads and trust, token scoping, lock staleness and release, --repo matching, move from any directory, census paging, and that no command takes a SHA.

groups.title: Skill, docs, and plan
intro: review-changes/SKILL.md replaces its start-comment, moved-head, and thread-query snippets with the commands and keeps their rules as what the commands guarantee. docs/cli.md gains a section on project review, and the plan's status becomes in-progress.

checks.text: Every rule the removed snippets carried survives either in the command or in the prose.
